name: AI-Native Software Engineering
audience: Working software engineers upskilling into AI-native development practice
philosophy: LEARN BY DOING. GROW THROUGH MENTORSHIP. AI assistance becomes a disclosed, verified, first-class part of professional engineering practice — never a shortcut around judgment, and never a reason to skip it.
assumptions: Apprentices are already working software engineers: they can write, test, and review code in at least one language, and they have a real project they can use as the substrate for these tasks.
Weekly hours assume this path runs alongside a job (about 5 hours of structured practice per week). A fully self-paced apprentice may move faster.
Tasks are language-agnostic. Use the stack you already ship in; do not invent a toy language just for this path.
aiPrinciples: AI assistance is disclosed on every task, not only when something goes wrong.
Critical review of AI-generated work is judged on what the apprentice verified, changed and rejected, not on whether AI was used.
The apprentice remains accountable for every submitted artifact, whether AI-assisted or independently produced.
Some tasks deliberately withhold AI solution generation because the judgment being assessed is knowing when not to reach for it.
Mentor approval is based on demonstrated verification and judgment, not on how polished the AI output looked.
